items.stem: A vendor shows an AI agent completing a multi-step task in a demo and claims it can now run business processes autonomously. Why treat this cautiously?

options.text: Demos are curated and current agents remain brittle, so broad autonomous reliability is not shown by a demo
options.rationale: Correct: a successful demo does not establish robust, general, production-ready autonomy.

options.text: Because AI agents never complete any task
options.rationale: Overstated: agents can complete some tasks; the issue is reliability and scope.

options.text: Because autonomy is banned by law everywhere
options.rationale: Inaccurate: the concern is evidence and risk, not blanket illegality.

options.text: Because demos always use fake software
options.rationale: Inaccurate and not the point; the issue is generalisation beyond the demo.

items.explanation: Correct: a successful demo does not establish robust, general, production-ready autonomy.

items.stem: Which TWO are sound ways to make an AI agent or reasoning system safer to use? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Add human checkpoints before the system takes consequential actions
options.rationale: Correct: human-in-the-loop review limits harm from errors.

options.text: Constrain its tools and scope and monitor what it does
options.rationale: Correct: limiting capabilities and observing behaviour are core guardrails.

options.text: Give it unlimited permissions so it can work faster
options.rationale: Unsafe: broad autonomy without limits increases risk.

options.text: Assume its step-by-step output proves it cannot be wrong
options.rationale: Incorrect: visible steps are not a guarantee of correctness.

items.explanation: Correct: human-in-the-loop review limits harm from errors.

items.stem: Why is step-by-step 'reasoning' output not proof that a model reasons like a human?

options.text: The visible steps are generated text that can look logical yet still be wrong or post-hoc
options.rationale: Correct: the format resembles reasoning but does not guarantee sound, human-like understanding.

options.text: Because models never produce useful intermediate steps
options.rationale: Overstated: such steps can help; they just are not proof of understanding.

options.text: Because only humans can write steps at all
options.rationale: Inaccurate: models clearly produce stepwise text.

options.text: Because reasoning output is always hidden from users
options.rationale: Inaccurate: it is often shown; visibility is not the issue.

items.explanation: Correct: the format resembles reasoning but does not guarantee sound, human-like understanding.
